subject: Discovery recap: latency & throughput constraints + proposed next steps
content:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: latency & throughput constraints + proposed next steps

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed mutual next steps so we have the same priorities. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Patient triage flows are very latency-sensitive: PU flow must return first token (streaming) within ~120ms for an acceptable UX.
- p95 for full responses should be <= 850ms for common prompts (length ~80 tokens); p99 can be higher but needs graceful UX handling.
- High concurrency during peak hours (clinic check-ins): roughly 450 concurrent sessions with burst to 900 for short windows.
- Current infra (on-prem Triton + hybrid inference via an older GPU fleet in us-west) is hitting memory fragmentation and inefficient batching for streaming scenarios.

Current stack (as you described):
- Primary: On-prem Triton for model hosting (custom wrapper) + Redis cache for embeddings
- Secondary: AWS GPU instances for overflow during daytime spikes (manual failover today)
- Orchestration: internal scheduler + a homegrown queuing layer

Success criteria you gave us (restated):
1) Consistent p95 <= 850ms for the core triage prompt set under expected peak load.
2) Streaming first-byte latency <= 120ms for conversational flows.
3) Support 450 sustained concurrent sessions, scale-to-900 bursts, with transparent fallbacks that don’t break the UX.
4) Clear per-token cost estimates and a path to reduce unit cost by >=20% via batching + cache.

Initial diagnosis (from today’s notes):
- The main blocker is the current batching policy and KV cache synergy with Triton; requests are often serialized in your scheduler which prevents efficient continuous batching.
- Tail latency is driven by a small subset of long-context requests (~5%) and by cold KV cache misses for prefix-heavy flows.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to run a short sizing exercise using your representative prompt set — please attach a sample prompt corpus and traffic profile (sample attached as acme_sizing.xlsx).
2) Technical deep-dive: 60–90 minute session with your infra leads + our runtime team to map actual RPCs and scheduler behavior. Attendees suggested: Karthik (runtime), Ben (solutions), your infra lead.
3) Proof-of-concept (2-week burst window): deploy a dedicated pool with streaming-optimized config to measure p95 and first-byte latency end-to-end.
4) Draft SLA / fallback policy: we’ll propose an SLA that includes automatic model-variant fallback (quantized variant) and region routing — initial draft attached (redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf).

Do these next steps align with your priorities? If so, we’ll schedule the sizing intake and technical deep-dive this week.

Thanks,
Sergio

All — quick internal notes and proposed plan from the runtime side:

Initial observations
- Continuous batching should get us >30% token-cost reduction for the triage flows if we can avoid the current scheduler serialization.
- Streaming first-byte at 120ms will require: tuned kernel selection for short-context attention, pre-warming KV caches for the 50 critical prompts, and a small dedicated pool pinned to low-latency instances (A100s or equivalent).

Proposed provenance/telemetry for the PoC
- Per-request: start_ts, first_byte_ts, end_ts, model_variant, cache_hit(bool), input_tokens, output_tokens.
- Aggregates: 50/95/99 latency percentiles, concurrency histogram per minute, error rates.

Short PoC plan (2 weeks)
1) Intake (2 business days): ingest the prompt corpus + traffic trace, Redwood creates the dedicated pool config.
2) Dry run (3 days): shadow traffic to the pool, validate metrics, run cold-start scenarios.
3) Live burst tests (2 days): coordinated test during Acme’s marketing push to validate scaling to 900 concurrency.
4) Wrap & SLO proposal (rest): finalize SLA text and cost model.

I’ve attached a quick sizing spreadsheet template (acme_sizing.xlsx) with the telemetry fields we’d need. I’ll sync with Karthik on kernel/config knobs.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
